# The same truncation as verify_truncate_workflow.txt, hidden behind a merge
# whose FIRST parent is an unrelated root commit. The history walk follows first
# parents, so it left the vault's history at that root and had nothing left to
# compare the shortened log against - truncation reported "ok". The walk has to
# cross over into the parent that still carries the log.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'c1'

# Snapshot the (short) c1 log; .gitignore keeps it untracked.
cp .sesam/audit/log.jsonl log-c1.jsonl

exec sesam add s.txt --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'c2'
exec sesam verify --truncate
stderr 'Audit log history: ok'

# Name the real history, then start an unrelated root and merge the vault into
# it: the merge's first parent is that root, the vault is only its second.
exec git branch vault
exec git switch --orphan unrelated
cp note note.txt
exec git add -f note.txt
exec git commit -m 'unrelated root'
# sesam's pre-merge-commit hook stops the merge short; finalize it without the
# hooks, so the fixture keeps exactly the merged tree.
! exec git merge --allow-unrelated-histories --no-edit vault
exec git commit --no-verify --no-edit

# Roll the log back to its c1 content inside the merge commit itself.
cp log-c1.jsonl .sesam/audit/log.jsonl
exec git add -A
exec git commit --amend --no-verify --no-edit

# The merge really does hang off an unrelated root...
exec git rev-list --first-parent HEAD
stdout -count=2 '^[0-9a-f]{40}$'

# ...and the shortened log must still be caught. no-disk isolates the history
# check from the on-disk root-hash mismatch the rollback also introduces.
! exec sesam --verify-mode no-disk verify --truncate
stderr 'not a prefix'

-- s.txt --
top secret
-- note --
unrelated file
